title: Herbarum varias qui vis cognoscere vires
shelf_note: Macer Floridus' verse herbal with a word-by-word prose commentary; a medieval medical botany fits a library of early science.
structure_note: The scan is a printed blackletter edition (a Baquelier imprint, with commentary), but 'published' reads 1150, the date the poem was composed, not when this edition was printed (I7, minor). Handwritten folio numbers (fol 44, fol 83) and signatures (f iij, l ii) run in order across the pages drawn. All 312 pages have OCR and translation.

title: Auriferae Artis, quam Chemiam vocant, Antiquissimi Authores

structure_note: Printed pages 315 (index 337) and 618 (index 670), then 260 (index 1002, ROSARIVM): the backstep matches the two separately paginated volumes of the 1572 edition bound into one record, so it is not a defect. 1,339 of 1,340 pages have OCR and 1,329 are translated.

title: De officiis. Comm: Petrus Marsus. Add: Laelius, sive de amicitia. Comm: Omnibonus Leonicenus; Cato maior, sive de senectute. Comm: Martinus Phileticus; Paradoxa Stoicorum
shelf_note: A 1486 incunable of Cicero's moral works with humanist commentaries; a classical primary source, though outside the esoteric core. No collection is set.
structure_note: Handwritten folio numbers 45, 91 and 137 rise in step with the page index, and the signature m iii is consistent. The pages are complex layouts: Cicero's text in a large-type block with commentary wrapped around it. The OCR and translation lose blocks of this layout: on p.93 the commentary column and one line of the main text are dropped, and on p.277 the whole Cicero text block is missing from the translation.

book_verdict: The incunable's layout of text block plus wraparound commentary defeats the pipeline. On p.93 a commentary column and a line of Cicero vanish from the OCR, on p.185 misreadings reverse the sense and turn the murdered father into the son, and on p.277 the English drops Cicero's own text entirely. An expert would flag it at once.

structure_note: Running heads (Primus, Quartus, Tractatus) and signatures (C ii, z iii) fit the order of the book. 150 of 157 pages are translated.

title: C. Velleii Paterculi Historiae. Romanae ad. M. Vinicium. cos. libri. 2 ab Aldo Manutio, Paulli f. Aldi n. emendati, et scholiis illustrati.

structure_note: Printed pages 47 and 104, then the scholia section (ALDI MANVTII, sig. L) at index 170, in the order the edition prints them. 227 of 228 pages have OCR and 222 are translated.
